page.layout: One printed page. Running head at top right with page number 61. Upper block: verse, one stanza, full width. Below it a rule, then a centred two-line heading in capitals, then a second verse stanza in italic, full width. No margin notes.

main_text.l: tiùs aut quisnam erranti per deuia turba
monstrauit itersuperas quod ducit in arces?
[?]ste igitur virtute, Hyperi, quem nec fera totū
ers domuit, totū seruant nec claustra sepulchri,
in superi meliore fouent iam parte receptum:
tera dū, tumulo qua nunc pars clausa, quiescit,
aminisque licèt iam cœli ad limen anhelat,
igilet felix: & quod tu diceris, illud
adas, Hyperi, tum re, tum nomine totus.

l.i: [?]quàm sana fuit tibi mens, Hallere, fuissent
Tam sana in vegeto corpore membra tibi:
[?]frueretur adhuc, qua te nùc, Berna, requirit,
Et tu plebe tua nunc fruereris adhuc:
tu tamen es vita felix meliore potitus,
st etiam unde suum soletur, Berna dolorem,
Orba suo quaꝶnuis iure parente gemat,
am quà in te vita exemplū duntaxat habebat,
Exemplum sanꝶa nunc quoque mortis habet.

page.notes: Line-initial letters of the first line and of the italic verse are cut off at the left edge and are uncertain. "ste" begins a word whose first letter is cut (virtute presumed). The page opens mid-stanza, so the first paragraph is a fragment. The heading's first letter is partly lost (IOANNIS presumed). Ornamental glyphs read as v (vegeto, virtute, vita, unde) and the sign for "quod" are interpreted from context. The italic stanza is printed as one block.
